items.title: Live: Two US planes shot down in Iran, 2 crew members rescued with one still missing
items.description: Two US planes have been shot down in Iran with 2 crew members rescued while another remains missing. Follow live.

items.title: World loses patience with Trump as war becomes about more than Iran
items.description: Global leaders are giving up the pretence of diplomatic niceties as they lose patience with the US president's actions.

items.title: The 20,000 sailors who have become sitting ducks in the Gulf
items.description: Interviews and first-hand accounts from sailors stranded in the Persian Gulf — under threat of drone attacks, missiles, and exploding boats — reveal an increasingly dire humanitarian crisis unfolding.

items.title: How the Iran war is pushing US ally the Philippines into economic crisis
items.description: Countries heavily reliant on imported oil are particularly vulnerable to the unfolding energy crisis caused by the US-Israel war with Iran. It's no more apparent than in South-East Asian countries like the Philippines.

items.title: Cops would not have had 'luxury' of taking Dezi Freeman alive, experts say
items.description: A former police hostage negotiator says he was sure Dezi Freeman's seven-month run from the law "was going to end in tears" and that the fugitive would never surrender.

items.title: Strategically critical Pacific island divided over growing US military presence
items.description: The Pacific Island of Guam sits at the centre of a struggle between the world's most powerful military and the right of its people to determine their own future.

items.title: Your pocket guide to daylight savings ending in Australia
items.description: The air is getting cooler and the days are about to get shorter as daylight savings comes to an end this weekend.

items.title: Considering downgrading your private health cover? These are the questions to ask
items.description: The loopholes to look for if you're thinking about downgrading or changing your private health insurance.

items.title: I find myself weeping again for Lebanon
items.description: Lebanese families have been told to flee homes that they might never be able to return to, and families are setting up tents for an uncertain and dangerous life on the streets of Beirut all because of a conflict not of their making, brought about by another state.

items.title: How nightmare Severe Tropical Cyclone Narelle became a historic storm
items.description: From the very first news reports about Severe Tropical Cyclone Narelle, it was clear this wasn't just another storm. This is the story of how the cyclone impacted the entire span of northern Australia and how communities came together to pick up the pieces.

items.title: 'So few precedents': One Nation leaves SA Liberals clinging to opposition status
items.description: The Liberal Party will have just one more seat than One Nation in South Australia’s lower house, leaving opposition leader Ashton Hurn little margin for error.

items.title: Nasal spray flu vaccines are here — but not all kids can get it for free
items.description: It's been available in the northern hemisphere for years, now Australian children can receive a nasal spray vaccine for the flu.

items.title: Poo of 'endearing' bat worth hundreds of millions, study says
items.description: Bats are often thought of as smelly, ugly and noisy, but a study has revealed the economic and ecological value of one Australian species's poo.

items.title: Voss unfazed about mounting speculation over his future as Blues coach
items.description: Michael Voss knows he faces more scrutiny over his role as Blues coach after his side endures another second-half meltdown.

items.title: 10 podcasts we can't stop listening to at the moment
items.description: The podcasts we're listening to this weekend include an investigation into the Salt Path scandal and a personal look at the role of Australia in the end of apartheid.

items.title: Gordi helped write a song for her partner, then 'stole it' back
items.description: Gordi's new single was originally meant to be for her partner. Thankfully, both artists know the importance of trusting their gut.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: A lost penguin, successful NASA rocket launch and address to the nation
items.description: It's been a big week in the news. Did you catch these stories?

items.title: 'Every word is delusional': Trump's speech lashed by former US envoy to Iran
items.description: Robert Malley, who negotiated the 2015 nuclear deal with Iran, says Donald Trump's address to the US this week was designed to deceive.

items.title: Judge dismisses Lively's sexual harassment claims against Baldoni
items.description: A US federal court judge tosses out Blake Lively's sexual harassment claims against It Ends With Us co-star Justin Baldoni, but leaves three more claims intact.

items.title: Art created for NT school reading program goes on display in Canberra
items.description: More than 40 years ago, a program was created to help Papunya children in remote NT learn to read in Pintupi-Luritja languages. Those books are now an insight into the people, stories, history and culture of the Papunya and are on display at the National Library of Australia.

items.title: Bellamy threatens to wield axe after Storm's humiliating loss to Panthers
items.description: Melbourne Storm coach Craig Bellamy puts his players on notice after they were thrashed 50-10 by Penrith on Good Friday.

items.title: Dockers claim thriller after Crow hits post inside final minute
items.description: Fremantle coughs up a five-goal lead before holding on in the final quarter after Adelaide's James Borlase hits the post with 30 seconds left on the clock.

items.title: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing elected president
items.description: In a live broadcast of the vote count the former commander-in-chief comfortably passed the threshold required to win the presidency.

items.title: Wet noses and silky coats helping to steady nerves ahead of court dates
items.description: Therapy dogs in courthouses are helping victims and witnesses of crimes to confront some of their darkest moments, but volunteers say many more are needed.

items.title: FIFA raises top ticket price for World Cup final to nearly $16,000
items.description: The top ticket price was $15,900, a sharp increase from the original $12,560 when FIFA sold tickets after the tournament draw in December.
